headline: Sachsen-Anhalt vorläufig: AfD 43.8% / 39 Sitze — absolute Mehrheit verfehlt; Amazon freighter kills 5 in Miami; Australia drafts algorithm opt-out.

stories.title: Sachsen-Anhalt: AfD 43.8% / 39 seats — majority missed; Musk “Well done!”
facts: Landeswahlleitung (vorläufiges Endergebnis, Nacht zum Montag): AfD 43.8% (39 of 83), CDU 17.2% (15), SPD 9.3% / Grüne 8.9% / Linke 8.6% (8 each), BSW 5.3% (5); FDP 2.6% out; turnout 77.8%.
Absolute majority needs 42 seats — AfD is three short; other parties together hold 44.
Evening Hochrechnung had AfD ~44.3% / ~41 seats — overnight count locked the miss and BSW’s entry.
Guardian: Musk wrote “Well done!” (German) to Weidel; Siegmund thanked him on X and floated “strong and constructive cooperation.”
tagesschau: BSW’s Thomas Schulze says he’ll talk to AfD (shared Russia/energy lines); Siegmund still rejects compromise coalitions and floats Neuwahlen.
France’s Europe minister Haddad called it a “serious moment”; Poland’s Tusk: only “idiots or traitors” rejoice.
stories.whyItMatters: Material overnight update: the knife-edge Hochrechnung is now a locked near-miss, so Magdeburg’s coalition math (and Berlin’s reaction) starts from 39—not 41—AfD seats, with Musk’s congratulations already in the international frame.

stories.title: Amazon Air freighter overruns Miami runway — 5 dead, 5 hurt
facts: BBC: Boeing 767-300 Amazon Air cargo (21 Air Flight 7598) from San Juan overshot MIA ~14:00 local / 19:00 GMT Sunday; hit ground vehicles and caught fire.
Miami-Dade mayor: at least 5 dead, 5 injured (3 critical per fire chief); 200+ firefighters; NTSB briefing planned Monday.
FlightRadar24: ~112 knots as it exited usable runway; Amazon’s Kelly Nantel offered condolences and pledged cooperation.
FAA grounded ops during Labor Day weekend at a top US freight hub.
stories.whyItMatters: A Prime Air–branded freighter killing ground workers next to an Amazon warehouse site puts logistics safety and contractor oversight on Monday’s NTSB mic.

image.alt: A Prime Air plane rests next to a car park after crashing. The nose of the plane is crumpled and there are black marks on the side of the plane.

stories.title: Australia: draft Digital Duty of Care would let users switch off algorithms
facts: BBC/ABC: Communications Minister Anika Wells to table exposure draft this week — platforms must offer algorithm opt-out (pop-ups: algorithmic vs following-only feed).
Duty of care would push platforms to identify/mitigate harm (illegal porn; youth psycho-social risks); breaches could mean fines >A$100m.
Wells still taking advice on opt-in vs opt-out default; opposition leader Angus Taylor is “deeply sceptical”; Greens want opt-in.
stories.whyItMatters: After the under-16 social-media ban, Canberra is moving from age gates to feed design — a template other regulators watch.

image.alt: A woman in a tartan jacket and white dress speaks. Several flags can be seen in the background

stories.title: China pumps ~$54bn into state banks and insurers
facts: BBC citing Xinhua: finance ministry-led package totals 360bn yuan (~$53.6bn) across eight state banks/insurers.
Named beneficiaries include ICBC, Agricultural Bank of China, China Export & Credit Insurance; aim is capital, risk buffers, and credit to the real economy.
Context: Q2 GDP 4.3% below annual target band; property slump + trade/tech rivalry with the US.
stories.whyItMatters: Beijing is using the fiscal balance sheet to pre-load bank/insurer capital before deeper growth stress shows up in credit.
